articles.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh: AFP journalists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: AFP journalists heard the blasts, and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an aerial threat

Multiple explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), as the military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
AFP journalists heard the blasts and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an "aerial threat".
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.
A subsequent message from the country's civil defence agency said the danger had passed.
The coalition had earlier said air defences also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.
On Sunday (November 8), the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an "attempted attack".

Images released by Saudi Arabia's press agency on Tuesday (November 10) showed the Riyadh region's deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company's headquarters.
The coalition has in response been launching airstrikes against Houthi positions inside Yemen.

According to Houthi news agency Saba, Saudi warplanes on Tuesday (November 10) carried out a series of strikes on the capital Sanaa and its outskirts, targeting a gas facility and a building belonging to the Yemeni state oil company.

articles.title: What are the eight Articles of impeachment filed against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Representative Thomas Massie, backed by lawmakers including Ro Khanna, has introduced eight Articles of Impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the House; here’s what you should know about them

There is a major shift happening in Capitol Hill following the U.S. midterm elections, as Representative Thomas Massie supported by lawmakers, including Representative Ro Khanna, introduced eight Articles of impeachment against U.S. Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth.
The Articles cite violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela.

Mr. Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend host and one of President Donald Trump’s handpicked appointees in his second term as U.S. President, took charge of the Department of War despite lacking administrative experience commensurate with the post. Despite controversies surrounding his tenure, Mr. Trump has maintained his support and repeatedly dismissed suggestions of dismissing him.
Here is the complete breakdown of the eight Articles of impeachment introduced in the formal House resolution.
Article 1 charges Mr. Hegseth with executing unlawful military orders by launching hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026.

The resolution states that the military strikes violated Section 2(c) of the 1973 War Powers Resolution because Congress had not declared war, provided statutory authorisation or faced any national emergency caused by an attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the U.S.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth to hold first Pentagon briefing since May amid impeachment threat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is scheduled to give his first news conference from the Pentagon in six months on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), just a day after a Republican lawmaker launched an effort to impeach him over his handling of the unpopular war against Iran and other actions.

The briefing will be Hegseth's first since May even as the U.S. military has kept up intermittent operations against the Islamic Republic as well as fatal strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America.

Mr. Hegseth, who has said the news conference would focus on the impeachment threat, is gearing up for a fight, having launched a social media blitz and saying he is ready to defend his and President Donald Trump's actions from “politically motivated people.”

Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican who lost his primary to a Trump-backed opponent, filed the impeachment resolution in the House on Monday (November 9). It sets the stage for a dramatic vote on whether to remove a prominent Trump administration figure following sweeping losses for Republicans in last week's midterm elections that many at least partly blamed on the Iran conflict and its economic impact.

The resolution largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Mr. Hegseth's role in military actions in Yemen against Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela. Massie said Hegseth's actions amount to “high crimes and misdemeanors” and his leadership at the Pentagon “warrants impeachment.”
A vote in the House could come by midweek, putting pressure on Republicans — many of whom blamed their election wipeout on the Iran war — but next steps are highly uncertain.

Mr. Trump has backed Hegseth, pointing to the raid to capture then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January as well as military operations against Iran that he asserts have “obliterated” its navy and air force.

Iran, however, has been able to keep striking U.S. military bases in West Asia and has disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz during the course of the more than 8-month-old conflict, driving up global oil prices. Mr. Trump told reporters on Monday (November 9) that the Iran war “militarily is effectively over" and repeated his often-made claim that Iran “would love to make a deal.”
Mr. Hegseth also has been defending his stewardship of the U.S. military.

“There's a lot of politically motivated people who may have substantial policy disagreements, but their disagreements are with success,” he told reporters on Monday (November 10) after a speech at the Naval War College in Rhode Island. He added that “if we want to litigate” the military actions that the Trump administration has taken, “I'm happy to do it all day long.”
He also released a video on social media last week that argued impeachment would be “all about the politics of personal destruction” and that “won't work with me. You can rest assured of that.”
Afterward, scores of Pentagon political appointees posted images of Hegseth emblazoned with the words, “Stand. Fight. Defend the Republic.”

articles.title: Republican Thomas Massie of Kentucky launches bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Thomas Massie, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Pete Hegseth's actions amounted to high crimes and misdemeanors

Rep Thomas Massie on Monday (November 9, 2026) moved to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing his fellow Republicans to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses blamed in part on fallout from the war in Iran.

Mr. Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read the impeachment resolution from the House floor just hours after it opened for the first day of sessions after the midterms. It largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth's role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela.
The Congressman, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Mr. Hegseth's actions amounted to “high crimes and misdemeanors.”
Mr. Hegseth, he said, “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” and “remains a threat to the Constitution.”
President Donald Trump lashed out at Massie personally just hours after the Congressman read the resolution, calling him a “loser” who “has a lot of hatred in his heart.”

A vote in the House could come by mid-week, but next steps are highly uncertain. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries supports the measure. If most Democrats follow him, Mr. Massie would only need support from a few Republicans to impeach Hegseth.

If the House votes to impeach, it would fall to to the Senate to either dismiss the charges or hold a trial. Republicans remain in the majority in both chambers, until the new Congress convenes in January with Democrats in control.
Sen Chuck Schumer, the Democratic leader, endorsed the impeachment push. "Hegseth must stand trial before the Senate," he said.

Republican leaders, who are eager to use their final weeks in power executing their own agenda, expressed frustration at the move. House Speaker Mike Johnson, who has tried to prevent the vote, said impeachment “in the middle of hostilities abroad would be a terrible, terrible look, a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see that.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he wasn't sure why the vote was being held now.
“We'll see what their ultimate decision is over there,” he said of the House. “We'll have to deal with it accordingly here."

Mr. Hegseth is stepping up his public statements ahead of the vote, telling reporters that he's eager to defend the military actions that he and Mr. Trump have taken against Iran, Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela's previous leaders.

articles.title: What is Megaspeed International, the firm under scanner over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.
Map showing the alleged locations of Megaspeed International | Photo Credit: Screengrab from LinkedIn

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. According to AFP , Megaspeed retorted in December of the same year, saying that Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

Jensen Huang, the top boss of the chip maker and one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship with Alice Huang. The Nvidia CEO said that he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife, my actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” the statement, uploaded on Nvidia’s website added.
The New York Times reported that Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang.

What is Megaspeed International, the firm under scanner over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.

Map showing the alleged locations of Megaspeed International | Photo Credit: Screengrab from LinkedIn

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.

The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.

All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. According to AFP , Megaspeed retorted in December of the same year, saying that Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

Jensen Huang, the top boss of the chip maker and one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship with Alice Huang. The Nvidia CEO said that he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife, my actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” the statement, uploaded on Nvidia’s website added.

The New York Times reported that Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang.

articles.title: Anthropic sends out, then retracts details of IPO filing, emails show
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Anthropic ‌sent out and ​then ⁠retracted details of its blockbuster IPO filing, ‌according to emails to bankers

Details of Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO, ​including plans by the AI company to raise nearly $70 billion, were briefly ⁠circulated to banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters.

A representative of Anthropic sent a copy of a securities filing that showed it aimed to sell about 867 ‌million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 per share, then followed up with an email saying details about the pricing were inaccurate. Anthropic said in ‌the second email it would update the filing later.
Anthropic declined to comment. The email ‌did ⁠not specify to bankers what was erroneous, and Reuters was unable to ⁠determine what was incorrect.

The original email whose details were retracted showed Anthropic planned to sell 866.7 million Class A shares, including a secondary offering. Anthropic itself would sell about 843.3 million shares, while existing shareholders would sell an additional ​23.3 million shares. The IPO would ‌raise $69.3 billion at the top of the range.

Separately, the original filing showed that Anthropic had lined up $26 billion in investments from some of the world’s biggest technology companies alongside its IPO, underscoring the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom.

Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, ‌Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC had agreed to participate in the ​private placement of Anthropic’s Class N common stock at the IPO price, which would close immediately after the IPO, the original filing showed.
Anthropic is ⁠expected to formally launch the roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected in the following week.

The Anthropic IPO comes at a time when other companies in the AI infrastructure and data center ‌sectors have delayed or withdrawn their planned listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave Inc and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, but expectations have since come down, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end of the range, Reuters previously reported.

Founded in ‌2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic’s president, Anthropic ​has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models.

The company’s rapid growth has been underpinned by Google and ⁠Amazon, which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as ⁠AI competitors.

Anthropic had nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, underscoring how its rapid growth depends on vast amounts of future capacity, some ‌of it reliant on financing beyond the company’s control.

articles.title: 331 tonnes of garbage removed from Madurai city after Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Madurai Corporation cleared a total of 331 tonnes of garbage, till 6 p.m. on Monday, which was generated across the city on Deepavali day.
Along with the corporation cleanliness workers, volunteers from the Democratic Youth Federation of India, joined the mass cleaning drive early on Monday morning.
Mayor (in-charge), T. Nagarajan, and Corporation Commissioner, Gaurav Kumar, inaugurated the cleanliness drive.

The drive started on the Chithrai Streets, Aavani Moola Streets, Masi Streets, Veli Streets and Vilakkuthoon junction around Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple where commercial establishments, especially textile showrooms, are located.
Besides, the workers focussed on spots at Teppakulam, Mattuthavani bus stand and Vaigai Bank Roads where garbage accumulation is higher.
Besides the usual vehicles used for transporting garbage, 11 earth movers, five bobcat machinery, nine tipper trucks and 42 tractors were involved in the exercise.

The work was expedited in the early hours so much so that 128.40 tonnes of garbage was cleared in the city by 12 noon. This was 33.32 tonnes of additional festival-time garbage removed when compared to 95.08 tonnes cleared during the same time in the last Deepavali season.
The workers had already removed 137 tonnes of garbage on Deepavali day (Sunday).
City Health Officer, Aravind Jothi, Assistant Health Officer, Abishek, DYFI district president, Selva, and secretary, Vel Deva, were present.

articles.title: FDA adds rare vision-loss warning to popular obesity, diabetes drugs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss and has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs,

Popular weight loss drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy will carry a new warning about a possible rare side effect that can sometimes lead to permanent vision loss, U.S. health regulators announced Monday, November 9, 2026.

The Food and Drug Administration said the risk will be added to the labelling of all GLP-1 drugs, the blockbuster medications used to treat obesity, diabetes and several other medical conditions. The class includes a dozen injectable or pill-based drugs, including widely used brands like Zepbound and Mounjaro.

The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss. The problem, which has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs, is caused by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve, although the underlying cause isn't understood, the FDA said.
FDA scientists began looking into the problem after the publication of a 2024 medical paper tying the condition to certain patients taking semaglutide, the active drug in Eli Lilly's Ozempic.

An FDA analysis of more than 125 clinical trials found that the problem occurred in roughly 6 of every 100,000 patients who took a GLP-1 for at least one year. The comparable rate for people taking a placebo or other types of glucose-lowering medications was less than 4 per 100,000, the FDA said.
The agency also found reports of the problem in its electronic reporting system for drug injuries and side effects.

Symptoms of the problem include blurred vision, blind spots, distorted colors and other visual disturbances, according to the FDA. Patients experiencing such problems should contact a health care professional immediately, the agency said.

articles.title: Andhra Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan to part ways with wife, Anna Lezhneva
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a joint statement, the couple said that, after sharing a significant part of their lives together, they had decided to separate
Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan and his wife Anna Lezhneva have decided to part ways “with mutual understanding and respect”.
In a joint statement shared with the media on Monday night (November 9, 2026), the couple said that, after sharing a significant part of their lives together, they had decided to separate.
“Though our marriage has come to an end, we remain good friends and devoted parents to our wonderful children. Their happiness and wellbeing will always remain our shared priority,” they said.
Mr. Kalyan and Ms. Lezhneva said they were seeking understanding, kindness and respect for their privacy during this personal transition.
They added that they were extending heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has stood by them throughout their journey.

Mr. Kalyan and Ms. Lezhneva married in September 2013. She is Russian and reportedly worked as a model and an actor. The couple has one daughter, Polena Anjana Pawanova, and one son, Mark Shankar Pawanovich.

articles.title: Award-winning Keralam farmer who used his banana farming as cover for smuggling drugs arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dhanesh S. Nair had allegedly trained members of his drug network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches
The Ernakulam Rural police have arrested an award-winning 31-year-old farmer suspected to be running a drug network under the cover of his agriculture ventures.

Dhanesh S. Nair, aka Dani, of Haripad, Alappuzha district was arrested with 803 grams of suspected hashish oil and 8 grams of suspected MDMA, the police said on Monday (November 9, 2026). The investigating team zeroed in on the accused as part of the probe into the recent arrest of Harikrishnan K.S., 32, of Palluruthy, Kochi with 185 gram of suspected MDMA from a lodge in Aluva.

The accused, who lives near Nanjanagudu, Mysuru, was nabbed by a special investigation team, led by District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarshan when he landed in Angamaly. The police suspect he was engaged in drug peddling under the cover of banana cultivation in Nanjanagudu.

He had reportedly pursued a higher education programme in Agribusiness in Germany between 2015 and 2018. He later returned to Keralam during the floods in 2018 and ventured into farming. The police said he had won a government award for the best young farmer in Haripad in 2022.

He had allegedly trained members of his network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches. Videos of the accused showing them methods to conceal drugs inside banana bunches were allegedly recovered from his mobile phone. The banana bunches were transported to Keralam under the guise of carrying agricultural produce. He had reportedly recruited youth to transport and distribute the drugs in Bengaluru and nearby areas. The drugs were later brought to Keralam and distributed among local suppliers and consumers.

Earlier, the police had held Shinu Sebastian, 34, of Thoppumpady with seven gram of suspected MDMA following the arrest of Mr. Harikrishnan. The police, sources said, suspect Mr. Harikrishnan and Mr. Sebastian were engaged in alleged drug peddling as per instructions given by Mr. Nair through social media.

Award-winning Keralam farmer who used his banana farming as cover for smuggling drugs arrested

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Dhanesh S. Nair had allegedly trained members of his drug network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches

The Ernakulam Rural police have arrested an award-winning 31-year-old farmer suspected to be running a drug network under the cover of his agriculture ventures.

Dhanesh S. Nair, aka Dani, of Haripad, Alappuzha district was arrested with 803 grams of suspected hashish oil and 8 grams of suspected MDMA, the police said on Monday (November 9, 2026). The investigating team zeroed in on the accused as part of the probe into the recent arrest of Harikrishnan K.S., 32, of Palluruthy, Kochi with 185 gram of suspected MDMA from a lodge in Aluva.

The accused, who lives near Nanjanagudu, Mysuru, was nabbed by a special investigation team, led by District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarshan when he landed in Angamaly. The police suspect he was engaged in drug peddling under the cover of banana cultivation in Nanjanagudu.

He had reportedly pursued a higher education programme in Agribusiness in Germany between 2015 and 2018. He later returned to Keralam during the floods in 2018 and ventured into farming. The police said he had won a government award for the best young farmer in Haripad in 2022.

He had allegedly trained members of his network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches. Videos of the accused showing them methods to conceal drugs inside banana bunches were allegedly recovered from his mobile phone. The banana bunches were transported to Keralam under the guise of carrying agricultural produce. He had reportedly recruited youth to transport and distribute the drugs in Bengaluru and nearby areas. The drugs were later brought to Keralam and distributed among local suppliers and consumers.

Earlier, the police had held Shinu Sebastian, 34, of Thoppumpady with seven gram of suspected MDMA following the arrest of Mr. Harikrishnan. The police, sources said, suspect Mr. Harikrishnan and Mr. Sebastian were engaged in alleged drug peddling as per instructions given by Mr. Nair through social media.

articles.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court says Delhi and the NCR bear the ‘cumulative burden of vehicular traffic’ and seeks to know what has been done to regulate in the capital the entry and plying of vehicles from neighbouring States

Forty-eight hours before Deepavali, amidst the rising crescendo of crackers heralding the festivities, a Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the people, and not the judiciary, must strike a blow against air pollution in the national capital.

Instead, the court went beyond Deepavali to highlight a consistent danger that sustains and would worsen the toxic air: vehicular emissions. On November 6, the court detected a sharp increase in issues attributable to vehicular emissions.

It told the authorities that the thick smog, which later raised the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) to almost the ‘severe’ category following Deepavali, had nowhere to go in the landlocked capital. The substantial commercial and non-commercial traffic entering Delhi would only compound the problem in the coming days.

“It must be borne in mind that Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), by virtue of their geographical and economic interconnectedness, bear the cumulative burden of vehicular traffic originating not merely within their own boundaries but also from the neighbouring States of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan,” the Supreme Court reminded the authorities in its latest order.

The issue warranted urgent and immediate intervention, the court said, directing the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), the Delhi government, the Delhi Police (Traffic department), as well as the neighbouring States of Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh to file their responses on what they have done to regulate in the national capital the entry and plying of commercial and non-commercial vehicles.

The court wanted to know about measures to regulate traffic originating from outside the national capital. These include steps taken to identify, monitor, and regulate vehicles that do not conform to prescribed emission standards, and measures to prevent the entry and operation of overage, end-of-life, or non-compliant vehicles.

The Bench has specifically sought information on the measures undertaken against violations, including the number of vehicles inspected, challaned, denied entry, and the coordination mechanisms between the authorities of Delhi and the neighbouring States for regulating inter-State vehicular movement.

The court has asked if the authorities have any “further short-term and long-term measures proposed or contemplated to mitigate vehicular emissions and reduce their contribution to the deteriorating air quality in Delhi and the National Capital Region”.

Incidentally, two separate orders of the Supreme Court passed several months ago, on January 21 and February 23 this year, had contained detailed long-term and short-term measures recommended by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to mitigate air pollution, especially caused by vehicular emissions, in Delhi.

The January 21 order had listed various CAQM recommendations, including phasing out polluting vehicles from Delhi-NCR, fortifying the pollution-under-check regime, augmentation of rail transport and metro models, revised electric vehicle policy, among others.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, for CAQM, had, at the time, submitted that a meta-analysis of studies from 2015 to 2025 attributed PM2.5 in Delhi to a mix of primary emissions and secondary particulate formation from sources within the national capital region itself. The measures suggested by the CAQM included developing multi-modal transport hubs connecting the metro, Regional Rapid Transit System, and last-mile connectivity with a real-time passenger information system, higher incentives to owners for scrapping old vehicles, expansion in EV charging infrastructure, etc.

“We direct the concerned agencies, particularly, the MCD, to submit their immediate response as to why these measures be not implemented without any delay. Once again, we clarify that no objections will be entertained against the recommendations made by the CAQM,” the court had made its intent clear on January 21.

articles.title: Keralam CPI(M) awaits ICC report on complaint against former Palakkad secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Complainant had made allegations of sexual misconduct against Babu; party State leadership to decide on further action based on findings in report

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has stepped up its internal inquiry into a sexual misconduct complaint against former Palakkad district secretary E.N. Suresh Babu. The party’s internal complaints committee (ICC) is investigating the complaint. It has reportedly completed key procedures, including recording the statement of the woman who filed the complaint.
The complainant is a lawyer and a party leader. She is understood to have submitted digital evidence in support of her allegations against Mr. Babu.

The ICC will submit its inquiry report and recommendations to the CPI(M) State committee after completing the investigation. The State leadership will decide on further action against Mr. Babu based on the findings. The possibility of disciplinary action, including removal from primary membership, is also being discussed within the party.

As per the party’s rules, a complaint against a leader of an organisational unit must be investigated by the ICC of the next higher committee. Since Mr. Babu was the Palakkad district secretary when the complaint was raised, the matter was referred to the ICC under the party central committee.

The woman’s complaint had earlier led to the intervention of the State leadership and Mr. Babu’s removal from the district secretary post. On October 4, the party appointed former MLA V. Chenthamarakshan as his successor at an extended district committee meeting. The CPI(M) had officially described the change as part of its organisational review following the electoral setback.

The party had maintained that Mr. Babu stepped down voluntarily due to personal reasons, denying any link between his removal and the complaint. However, the ICC inquiry has brought the circumstances surrounding his exit as district secretary back into focus.
The complaint reportedly relates to an incident at the CPI(M) district committee office in Palakkad, where the woman had been called.

The issue is likely to come up for further discussion at the State leadership level after the ICC submits its report. The findings and recommendations will determine the next course of action against Mr. Babu.

articles.title: Oxford University returns remains of 39 Naga people after more than a century
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on November 9, 2026
The University of Oxford returned the remains of 39 members of the Naga community, which were held at its Pitt Rivers Museum for more than a century, in a historic repatriation initiative.
The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR) and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The transfer of title document was signed by Pitt Rivers Museum Director Professor Laura Van Broekhoven and FNR representative Rev. Dr. Wati Aier. It was witnessed by Visier Sanyu on behalf of the FNR and Thejao Vihienuo representing the Naga Tribe Hoho.
Following the handover, the ancestral remains were moved from the University of Oxford to begin their journey to Nagaland, according to a statement issued by the FNR on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

The remains had been part of the collections of the Pitt Rivers Museum, established in 1884, which houses cultural artefacts collected from various parts of the world. Addressing the ceremony, University of Oxford Vice-Chancellor Professor Irene Tracey described the handover as a historic moment in the relationship between the university and the Naga people.
“She said the initiative reflected a community-led effort towards reconciliation, healing and peace,” the statement said.

Mr. Sanyu spoke about the impact of British colonial violence on Naga communities and recounted how his own village was burnt by colonial forces. Emphasising the importance of forgiveness and reconciliation, he quoted late Naga peace activist Niketu Iralu as saying, "Hate not transformed is transferred".

Thejao Vihienuo, president of the Angami Public Organisation, who represented the Naga Tribe Hoho, said the return of the ancestral remains was the right of the Naga people to care for their ancestors. He called for the return of all Naga ancestral remains held in museums to their homeland with dignity.
Meanwhile, preparations have begun for the burial of the remains at Naga Solidarity Park in Kohima. The Naga Solidarity Park Management Committee has allocated a designated site within the park.
A prayer service was recently held at the park to mark the formal commencement of preparatory work for the proposed burial site, the committee's convenor Vipopal Kintsi said.
“The proposed burial is intended to provide a common resting place for the ancestral remains and promote healing, reconciliation and unity among the Naga people,” he said.
Mr. Kintsi said the homecoming of the remains should transcend historical and tribal divisions and strengthen a shared sense of Naga identity.

articles.title: Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s bail plea dismissed in alleged multi-crore private school bribery case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Anbil Mahesh was arrested on October 26 and remanded in judicial custody till November 18

A special court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the bail petition filed by former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, who is accused of receiving a share of an alleged multi-crore bribe collected from private school managements allegedly through threats, deception, and false promises of securing government approvals.

D.C. Elangovan, secretary of the Private School Management Association, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Commissioner of Police on June 23, 2026, alleging that nearly ₹100 crore had been collected from private school managements through intimidation and forgery.

The complaint named B.T. Arasakumar (Accused 1), who allegedly floated an unregistered body called the Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association (TNPSA), claiming to be its founder-president, and Muthukumar (Accused 2), a former MLA from Virudhachalam, as the key persons involved in the collection of bribes.

The two allegedly organised an event of the TNPSA at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024, which Mr. Poyyamozhi attended as the chief guest. The prosecution alleged that a bank account was subsequently opened in the name of BTK Educational Development Trust at the Canara Bank’s Tondiarpet branch; this account was used to collect membership fees and other amounts from private schools.

The FIR alleged that the accused assured school managements that they could obtain government approvals and permissions easily, even if their institutions lacked basic requirements. They allegedly threatened that schools refusing to pay the demanded amounts would not receive the necessary permissions, potentially affecting students appearing for the SSLC and Class XII public examinations.

Dismissing the bail petition, Special Court Judge L.S. Sathiyamurthy noted that statements from witnesses, including private school correspondents and managers, had been recorded by the investigating officer and before the Judicial Magistrate. “A preliminary examination of these statements indicated a prima facie link between the petitioner and the alleged offence,” the judge observed.

The investigating agency had also seized computers and other digital devices from Mr. Poyyamozhi’s premises and sent them to a forensic laboratory for examination. The court said it would have to await the findings of the cyber forensic experts.

Observing that the investigation was still at an early stage and the first period of remand had only just concluded, the Special Court Judge said the materials collected so far indicated that substantial sums had been extorted from multiple private school managements through deception and threats. Witness statements suggested that money collected by A1, A2, and their associates had reached the petitioner under the guise of a ‘party fund’, it said.

Classifying the case as a multi-crore economic offence involving several victims, the court pointed out that some of the accused were yet to be arrested and the custodial interrogation of Muthukumar who had surrendered after the arrest of Mr. Poyyamozhi and other accused, was at an initial stage.

The court also underscored the responsibility attached to public office, observing that the petitioner, as School Education Minister, had been entrusted with the welfare of students, teachers, and parents.

Holding that public interest, particularly the welfare and education of schoolchildren, outweighed the petitioner’s (Mr. Poyyamozhi) claim for bail at this stage, Mr. Sathiyamurthy dismissed the petition.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 10 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s bail plea dismissed in alleged multi-crore private school bribery case

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Anbil Mahesh was arrested on October 26 and remanded in judicial custody till November 18

A special court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the bail petition filed by former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, who is accused of receiving a share of an alleged multi-crore bribe collected from private school managements allegedly through threats, deception, and false promises of securing government approvals.

D.C. Elangovan, secretary of the Private School Management Association, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Commissioner of Police on June 23, 2026, alleging that nearly ₹100 crore had been collected from private school managements through intimidation and forgery.

The complaint named B.T. Arasakumar (Accused 1), who allegedly floated an unregistered body called the Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association (TNPSA), claiming to be its founder-president, and Muthukumar (Accused 2), a former MLA from Virudhachalam, as the key persons involved in the collection of bribes.

The two allegedly organised an event of the TNPSA at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024, which Mr. Poyyamozhi attended as the chief guest. The prosecution alleged that a bank account was subsequently opened in the name of BTK Educational Development Trust at the Canara Bank’s Tondiarpet branch; this account was used to collect membership fees and other amounts from private schools.

The FIR alleged that the accused assured school managements that they could obtain government approvals and permissions easily, even if their institutions lacked basic requirements. They allegedly threatened that schools refusing to pay the demanded amounts would not receive the necessary permissions, potentially affecting students appearing for the SSLC and Class XII public examinations.

Dismissing the bail petition, Special Court Judge L.S. Sathiyamurthy noted that statements from witnesses, including private school correspondents and managers, had been recorded by the investigating officer and before the Judicial Magistrate. “A preliminary examination of these statements indicated a prima facie link between the petitioner and the alleged offence,” the judge observed.

The investigating agency had also seized computers and other digital devices from Mr. Poyyamozhi’s premises and sent them to a forensic laboratory for examination. The court said it would have to await the findings of the cyber forensic experts.

Observing that the investigation was still at an early stage and the first period of remand had only just concluded, the Special Court Judge said the materials collected so far indicated that substantial sums had been extorted from multiple private school managements through deception and threats. Witness statements suggested that money collected by A1, A2, and their associates had reached the petitioner under the guise of a ‘party fund’, it said.

Classifying the case as a multi-crore economic offence involving several victims, the court pointed out that some of the accused were yet to be arrested and the custodial interrogation of Muthukumar who had surrendered after the arrest of Mr. Poyyamozhi and other accused, was at an initial stage.

The court also underscored the responsibility attached to public office, observing that the petitioner, as School Education Minister, had been entrusted with the welfare of students, teachers, and parents.

Holding that public interest, particularly the welfare and education of schoolchildren, outweighed the petitioner’s (Mr. Poyyamozhi) claim for bail at this stage, Mr. Sathiyamurthy dismissed the petition.

articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process
Several industry bodies have urged the Ministry of Finance to rationalise long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equities and reduce securities transaction tax (STT) in the upcoming Union Budget 2027.

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been holding pre-Budget consultative meetings with the main industry bodies such as the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), and the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI).

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was to rationalise LTCG tax on equities, particularly in view of the tax concessions extended to certain debt instruments. However, several other tax proposals related to the capital market also feature in the recommendations.

The PHDCCI, for example, has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about ₹3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

Budget 2027 will be presented against the backdrop of the ongoing West Asia crisis, rising inflation, and fiscal pressure on the government. In this, India’s micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) need help, the industry bodies have argued.

Towards this, PHDCCI has requested the Finance Minister to extend the overdue period for classifying a loan as a non-performing asset (NPA) from the existing 90 days to 180 days. The move, it argued, would “accommodate longer working capital cycles and delayed realisation of receivables”.

Further, the chamber has called for an enhancement of PM MUDRA loan limits and a Budget announcement of direct equity support to MSMEs through the Fund of Funds Scheme, “with dedicated allocations for start-up seed capital and SME IPO participation.

articles.title: Malaysian court clears final hurdle for former PM Najib Razak's transfer to house arrest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “A High Court in Malaysia on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) cleared all legal hurdles for the transfer of imprisoned former Prime Minister Najib Razak to his home to serve the remainder of his graft sentence under house arrest,” his lawyer said.
Najib has been behind bars since August 2022, when the Kuala Lumpur High Court upheld his graft conviction linked to a multibillion-dollar looting of the state investment fund 1MDB.
In September, Najib was granted royal clemency, allowing him to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest once he pays a court-imposed fine.

Last Friday, he left prison after his political party paid the 50 million ringgit ($12.3 million) fine but he was brought back hours later after the attorney general blocked the transfer, seeking legal clarifications.

The attorney general's request sparked a public rebuke from the palace, which said that King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar's prerogative of pardon for Najib that allowed the house arrest was clear and must be respected. It said any attempts to challenge it would amount to defying the royal order.

Najib's lawyer Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said on Tuesday all was settled for the former Prime Minister's transfer to house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur home, where he is to remain until Aug 23, 2028. Najib appeared in court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026); the transfer was expected to take place later in the day. Police later sealed off the road leading to his home. “It's a final relief, you know, great sigh to him because he has been waiting for this,” the lawyer said.

The house arrest covers only Najib's reduced, six-year sentence in his first trial for graft and not a separate, 15-year sentence handed down last December for corruption and money laundering. That sentence followed a second major trial tied to the 1MDB scandal.
Najib is also appealing that sentence, which he is to serve after the end of his first sentence. If his appeal fails, he could return to prison after his house arrest ends.

Najib, who served as Prime Minister from 2009 to 2018, has denied any wrongdoing. He is Malaysia's first former leader to be imprisoned under a sentence related to the 1MDB scandal. It marked one of the world's largest financial scandals, rippling across global markets and triggering investigations in the United States and other countries.

articles.title: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Hasina will be executed if she returns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,’ Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.
The Bangladeshi prosecutor who secured the death sentence against ousted leader Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) she will be executed if she returns home.

Ms. Hasina, whose 15-year rule was ended by a mass uprising she tried to crush, has vowed to return in December to Bangladesh, where she was convicted of crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters.
"Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict," Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.
He added that the 79-year-old fugitive had missed the deadline to appeal against her conviction, leaving her with no further legal recourse.
"The statutory appeal period has expired, and no appeal can now be filed," he said.

The daughter of a revolutionary who led Bangladesh to independence in 1971, Ms. Hasina presided over breakneck economic growth, helping transform the South Asian nation of 170 million people from a largely agricultural economy into a global manufacturing hub.
Critics have accused Ms. Hasina of jailing political rivals, enacting harsh anti-press laws and overseeing widespread human rights abuses, including the killing of opposition activists.
Her 2024 crackdown left up to 1,400 people dead, according to the United Nations.
She fled to neighbouring India by helicopter in August 2024 as angry crowds stormed her palace.
She has remained there ever since, hidden from public view. Only occasionally has she addressed news conferences by telephone, her voice sounding frail.
Ms. Hasina has repeatedly said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December, telling AFP she is "fully aware" she faces being hanged if she returns.
She said "fear cannot decide" her "duty to the people".

articles.title: Poland arrests two Ukrainians over alleged Russian espionage, sabotage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine
Poland has arrested two Ukrainian men suspected of espionage ​and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence ‌services, the Internal Security Agency (ABW) ​said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia has repeatedly ‌denied the accusations.

“According to findings ‌by ⁠the ABW, the suspects carried ⁠out tasks on behalf of Russian special services, which included, among other things, reconnoitring critical infrastructure ​and military facilities ‌throughout the country,” the agency said in a statement.

“The prosecutor has charged both detainees with engaging in espionage activities ‌on behalf of a foreign ​intelligence service against the Republic of Poland, as well as ⁠committing acts of sabotage.”

According to investigators, the men set fire to vehicles after replacing ‌their licence plates with ones resembling those used by the Ukrainian military. The men were paid for carrying out the tasks, including in cryptocurrencies.

“The investigation has established that the ‌acts of sabotage were carried out at the ​behest of Russian intelligence services and were intended to fuel anti-Ukrainian ⁠sentiment,” prosecutors said in a separate statement.
Both ⁠face from 10 years to life imprisonment if found guilty.
The Russian ‌embassy in Warsaw did not immediately respond to an emailed request ​for comment.

fullParagraphs: Meghan Markle recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father's former home

Thomas Markle, the father of Prince Harry's wife Meghan, was arrested on Friday morning (November 6, 2026) by federal agents in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material, people familiar with the matter told The Associated Press.
U.S. judge orders psychiatric exam for Meghan Markle's father
The people who confirmed his arrest were not authorised to publicly discuss the investigation and spoke on the condition of anonymity. Thomas Markle was taken into custody near Tampa.

Meghan Markle recently said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father's former home. She also revealed that a letter containing “troubling allegations” about him had been sent to London police in 2018.
Meghan, an American citizen who starred in the U.S. television drama Suits , married Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.

Her father, a retired television lighting and photography director, did not attend the wedding, prompting extensive coverage in the British media of Meghan's estrangement from her father. Meghan said she decided to distance herself from him to protect her children.

articles.title: Kadambini Ganguly: breaking barriers in medicine
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: In her time, Kadambini Ganguly challenged convention to become the first Indian female doctor to practice Western medicine

Have you heard of the names Kadambini Ganguly and Anandibai Joshi? Considered India’s first female doctors, these names have often been looked past in the pages of history and even medical textbooks. Today, let’s talk about the story of Kadambini Ganguly — India’s first practising lady doctor.

It was in 1861 that Brahmo reformer and headmaster Braja Kishore Basu had a daughter. She was named Kadambini Basu. Young Kadambini, despite hailing from a community that did not necessarily support women’s education like many others at the time did, received an education at the Brahmo Eden Female School and later at the Hindu Mahila Vidyalaya.

As the daughter of someone who organised and fought for women’s emancipation, Kadambini went on to study in college and became the first woman to pass the University of Calcutta entrance examination. In 1882, she passed the examination for the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree along with Chandramukhi Basu from the University of Calcutta, making her and Chandramukhi the first female graduates in the country.

Wanting to study medicine, Kadambini decided to enrol at the Calcutta Medical College after graduation. She was, however, believed to have been unable to receive the BMC certificate due to a shortage of a couple of marks. She did receive the GBMC (Graduate of Bengal Medical College) degree, though, in 1886. Thus, she became the first Indian woman to be allowed to practice Western medicine.

Around 1888, Kadambini started working at the Lady Dufferin Hospital for a monthly salary of 300 rupees. She had even gone to Nepal to treat British royalty. Along with pursuing medicine, she was also politically quite vocal and active. Around 1899, Kadambini was one of the first women delegates elected to the Fifth Session of the Congress in Bombay and the next year, she won to become the first women speaker at the Congress.

She also served as the president of the Transvaal Indian Association, founded by Gandhiji’s colleague Henry Pollock. She was a member of the Women’s Conference held in Calcutta and even presided over the General Brahmo Samaj session in Calcutta.

Around 1883, Kadambini married Dwarakanath Ganguly (thus the change in name from Kadambini Bose to Kadambini Ganguly in many documents). Dwarakanath Ganguly was a Bengali Brahmo reformer, educator, journalist, and pioneer of women’s rights in British India.

She was a mother to eight children and is often said to have been deft in needlework. She became a practising doctor while equally devoting herself to family and household affairs, an action which was deemed impossible by many in the era.

Despite having being burdened with domestic chores, like most women of that time, Kadambini still managed to smash the glass ceilings and societal stereotypes in both her professional and personal life.
A name which should not be forgotten in the course of time, Dr Kadambini is a reason many of us are able to pursue our passion — in medicine and in life.

articles.title: BJP sets sights on grassroots expansion ahead of A.P. panchayat polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: State president P.V.N. Madhav urges leaders to secure a presence in every village and panchayat, building on the party’s gains in municipal corporations, ZPTCs and MPTCs

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has identified the forthcoming panchayat elections as an opportunity to strengthen its presence across Andhra Pradesh, with State president P.V.N. Madhav urging party leaders to ensure representation in every village and panchayat.

Addressing a State-level workshop on local body election results, Mr. Madhav said the BJP had secured representation in all 13 municipal corporations that went to polls in the first phase. It had won about 23 of the 33 ZPTC seats contested and secured MPTC seats. Around 355 party representatives had been elected across the State, he said.

The three-phase panchayat elections, scheduled for November 13, 17 and 19, were crucial to expanding the party at the grassroots. He called for stronger coordination among alliance partners and effective utilisation of Central funds released to panchayats.

BJP national vice-president and Rajamahendravaram MP Daggubati Purandeswari attributed the party’s electoral gains to the efforts of generations of workers. The BJP had won more than 59% of the seats allotted to it under the alliance arrangement, she said.
Citing its performance in the erstwhile combined East Godavari district, she said the party had won 10 of 11 seats in Anaparthi, all three in Gopalapuram and both seats allotted to it in Kovvur.
She urged elected representatives to remain accessible to party workers and called for grooming a new generation of leaders to take the organisation forward over the next 10 to 15 years.

articles.title: Mannarkkad gears up to host Kerala State school science fair from November 18
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: More than 7,000 students expected to take part in event; Minister Samsudheen chairs review meeting to assess preparations made by various committees, subcommittees
The 58th State school science fair will be held at Mannarkkad from November 18 to 21. More than 7,000 students are expected to take part in the fair.
General Education Minister N. Samsudheen unveiled the logo of the fair at a function held at Darunnajath Higher Secondary School, Nellipuzha, Mannarkkad, on Tuesday.

The Minister also chaired a review meeting to assess the preparations made by various committees and subcommittees. He asked the committees to ensure that all facilities, including accommodation and food, were arranged for the participating students and teachers. He also sought the cooperation of all sections to make the event a success.

The mathematics fair will be held at Kalladi Higher Secondary School, Kumaramputhur; the social science fair at MET Higher Secondary School, Mannarkkad; the work experience fair at Darunnajath Higher Secondary School, Nellipuzha; and the science and IT fairs at MES Higher Secondary School, Mannarkkad.

The Young Innovators Programme (YIP) Sasthrapadham idea exhibition will also be held at MES Higher Secondary School. The skill festival exhibition and career fest will be organised at Mini Mubas Stadium at Nellipuzha. The skill festival will be held at GMUP School, Mannarkkad.
The fair will be organised in compliance with green protocol. Temporary traffic regulations will be introduced to ensure smooth movement of vehicles. Cultural programmes will be held every evening.

K. Premkumar, MLA, presided over the function. Mannarkkad municipal chairperson K. Sajna, block panchayat president Neethu Shankar, Education department officials, programme committee representatives and headteachers of various schools attended.

articles.title: Domestic rooftop solar installations in T.N. remain low due to policy challenges, say consumers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With 425.61 MW of domestic rooftop solar installations in Tamil Nadu that have benefited from the PM Surya Ghar scheme, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation is taking efforts to bring more households under rooftop solar.
However, industry and consumer representatives say the State government should address a couple of basic policy issues so that more households go in for rooftop solar.

“While the government advertisements claim that consumers will get to pay nothing as bi-monthly energy charges if they instal rooftop solar, in reality, they have to pay network charges,” says K. Kathirmathiyon, secretary of Coimbatore Consumer Cause.

A.D. Thirumurthi, advisor of the National Solar Energy Federation of India, says the consumers should be exempted from network charges for rooftop solar. Further, in the case of additional solar energy generated in a financial year that goes unused, the consumers should be paid at least the average power purchase cost for the excess solar energy they feed to the grid.

Mr. Kathirmathiyon explained that if a consumer instals a five KW rooftop solar and his bi-monthly consumption is 500-550 units, he will supply the excess to the grid. He does not get any payment for the additional power. Instead, he will have to pay nearly ₹5,800 annually as network charges. Why should a consumer pay for solar energy that he has generated and not consumed, he asks.

“Tamil Nadu should adopt an approach similar to Kerala instead of allowing surplus electricity credits to lapse without compensation. Network charges applicable to domestic rooftop solar investors under the TNERC tariff framework with effect from October 22, 2021 constitute another major disincentive,” he says.

The Government and the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission should ensure domestic rooftop solar power producer/consumer is paid for the surplus electricity remaining unadjusted at the end of the settlement period (31st March). It should also withdraw network/wheeling charges levied on domestic rooftop solar power producers.
Mr. Thirumurthi says residents who consume more than 500 units of electricity in two months stand to benefit more if they go in for solar. The government should take steps to encourage them, he said.

articles.title: Guntur DRO calls for accuracy, coordination among officials during Census 2027 exercise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing a training session, N.S.K. Khajavali stresses the need for officials to develop a thorough understanding of the census process and to effectively implement the procedures learned during field-level training

District Revenue Officer (DRO) N.S.K. Khajavali has directed officials to make comprehensive preparations for the Census 2027 exercise and ensure accuracy, coordination and accountability at every stage of the enumeration process. The DRO was addressing officials at the concluding session of a two-day training programme on Phase-II census data collection at Sankaran Hall in Guntur Collectorate on Tuesday.
The training programme, held on November 9 and 10, was attended by district census officers, mandal-level charge officers, additional charge officers, census clerks and technical assistants.

Mr. Khajavali stressed the need for officials to develop a thorough understanding of the census process and to effectively implement the procedures learned during field-level training. He said that accurate data collection and coordinated efforts among departments were essential for the successful conduct of the exercise.

articles.title: India Post being modernised with focus on technology, customer service: Pemmasani
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union Minister inspects post offices and BSNL infrastructure in Bhopal; stresses faster postal services and improved connectivity

India Post is being comprehensively modernised through the adoption of advanced technology and a customer-centric approach to deliver faster and better-quality services, Union Minister of State for Communications Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar said.

According to a press release issued by the Minister’s camp office in Guntur, Dr. Chandra Sekhar made the remarks during surprise inspections of two major post offices in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, on Tuesday. He said the postal department was being strengthened to function with the efficiency and service standards of a corporate organisation while retaining public trust.

He inspected counter services, ticketing systems, parcel delivery networks, mail handling and other modern facilities. He also interacted with postal employees to understand their workplace challenges and requirements and sought feedback from customers and members of the public on service quality and the problems they faced.

He said India Post had evolved beyond letter delivery into a major public service network offering banking and insurance facilities. Efforts to strengthen its operations had been intensified over the past two-and-a-half years.
He highlighted the expansion of banking services through India Post Payments Bank and the digital transformation of Postal Life Insurance.
Later, he reviewed BSNL’s network and technical infrastructure in Bhopal and directed officials to ensure uninterrupted high-speed connectivity and improve telecommunications services.

articles.title: U.S. President Donald Trump nominates Natalie Baker as next Ambassador to Pakistan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ms. Baker is currently serving as charge d’affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad. She assumed the role in January 2025, following the departure of then-ambassador Donald Armin Blome

U.S. President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker to be the next U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan , paving the way for the appointment of a permanent envoy to Islamabad after a gap of nearly two years, it emerged on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
Ms. Baker is currently serving as charge d’affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad. She assumed the role in January 2025, following the departure of then-ambassador Donald Armin Blome.

The White House, in a statement, said the nomination has been submitted to the U.S. Senate, whose foreign relations committee will review it. If approved by the committee, the nomination will proceed to a vote by the full Senate. Ms. Baker would be appointed as the U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan following the Senate’s confirmation.

Earlier, she had arrived in Islamabad as Deputy Chief of Mission in August 2024, according to details available on the embassy’s website. Prior to that, she served as the Deputy Chief of Mission at the U.S. Embassy in Doha from August 2021 to July 2024.

Ms. Baker was also deployed as the Deputy Chief of Mission and charge d’affaires of the U.S. Mission to Libya, deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office at the U.S. consulate in Dubai and economic counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Kuwait.

She also served as the director of the Office of North African Affairs in the U.S. State Department’s Near Eastern Affairs Bureau. Ms. Baker is quite active in Islamabad and frequently interacts with local officials and the political leadership of Pakistan. She also oversaw the marked improvement in ties between Pakistan and the U.S. during the tenure of President Trump.

articles.title: Zelensky holds air defence, energy security talks with Nordic leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Nordic countries are among the main supporters of Ukraine and Zelensky travelled to Oslo at the end of October to meet with American envoys

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) arrived in Denmark to discuss military support, air defence and energy infrastructure security with Nordic leaders, Danish authorities said.

"I am proud to welcome President Zelensky and the Nordic leaders to Denmark. The Ukrainians' fight for a free Ukraine and a free Europe continues," Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said in a statement.
The Nordic countries are among the main supporters of Ukraine and Zelensky travelled to Oslo at the end of October to meet with American envoys.
Direct negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow, under U.S. mediation, also began on Tuesday (November 10) in Abu Dhabi.
"Almost five years after the full-scale invasion, the rain of bombs targeting civilians, relief centres, and water and heating plants continues. That is why we must stand firm," Mr. Frederiksen said.

Copenhagen police announced Tuesday (November 10) that they would increase security in public spaces for the coming days. They have introduced a ban on the use of drones over the capital until November 12.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. court allows Pannun to serve NSA Doval and former intelligence chief Goyal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Order issued on November 9, 2026, after State department attempts to serve Indian officials via Embassy, MEA rejects charges as “frivolous”, calls Pannun’s case “fabricated and malicious”

A U.S. court on Monday (November 9, 2026) allowed Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to serve his civil plea on National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former R&AW intelligence chief Samant Goel through Indian judicial channels, after the State Department submitted that it had served the notice for the two officials at the Indian Embassy in Washington.

The move was rejected by the Ministry of External Affairs, which said such judicial documents must go to the Ministry of Law and Justice in India and called Mr. Pannun’s civil lawsuit “frivolous”. The lawsuit filed by Mr. Pannun, who is wanted in India on terror charges, is separate but linked to the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)’s findings of an assassination plot against Mr. Pannun in June 2023. An undercover Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) informant had pointed to Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, and to conversations with senior Indian intelligence officials including Vikash Yadav for a conspiracy to hire a hitman to kill Mr. Pannun in New York. Mr. Gupta has subsequently pleaded guilty to all the charges, and the courts have set November 20 as the date for his sentencing. Mr. Yadav was arrested in Delhi in December 2023 on separate charges by Indian authorities and given bail in April 2024.

The FBI in the U.S. and Canadian officials investigating a similar case involving the killing of Harjeet Singh Nijjar in Vancouver in June 2023 appear to have dropped earlier claims of the involvement of more senior officials, including NSA Doval, former R&AW chief Samant Goyal, and Home Minister Amit Shah. However, Mr. Pannun has sought to pursue his case further and has filed several petitions demanding that Mr. Doval and Mr. Goyal be summoned by the court. In February 2025, when Mr. Doval accompanied Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Washington for a bilateral visit and meeting with US President Donald Trump, Mr. Pannun had tried to serve the NSA with a notice and failed.

The Ministry of External Affairs indicated on Tuesday (November 10) that it was unconcerned by the latest development in the case, and that the procedure for issuing the notice would require engaging the Law Ministry directly, not via the Embassy or the MEA.

“We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials, as also we reject the frivolous lawsuits. Request for serving of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India’s designated central authority, that is the Ministry of Law and Justice,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to questions at a regular briefing.

Granting permission for the summons on Monday (November 9), U.S. District Judge Katherine Polk Failla directed Mr. Pannun to prepare a number of documents on or before November 30, including the summons addressed to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goyal, details of Indian law and procedure and the route by which the summons would be issued, as well as records of previous attempts at serving the two officials under the Hague Convention.

The certificate of submission delivered to the Indian Embassy by the State Department was signed by an official and dated October 9, 2026. Neither the Embassy nor the MEA had commented on the issue. The State Department said in a footnote that the delivery did not mean it was taking a “position” on the case and was a “legal obligation.
