articles.title: West Bengal to institute 'Seema Mitra' award for BSF, SSB, police personnel from 2027: Suvendu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 8, 2026) announced that his government would institute the 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 to recognise exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB, and state police personnel in securing the country's borders.

A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh.
"We will give the 'Seema Mitra' award from next year for BSF, SSB and West Bengal police personnel," Mr. Adhikari said.
The Chief Minister visited the border outpost to greet security personnel on the occasion of Diwali and Kali Puja.
The BSF guards the India-Bangladesh border, while the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is deployed along the country's frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan.
Mr. Adhikari apologised to the BSF and CRPF personnel for what he described as derogatory remarks and behaviour by the previous State government.

"I, as the Chief Minister of the State, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF," he said, targeting the erstwhile Trinamool Congress government.
He alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee government had failed to provide the required land to the BSF for fencing nearly 600 km of the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal.
Mr. Adhikari said the BJP government had handed over the required land to the BSF soon after assuming office and would provide any additional land needed for border fencing.
He said that his government will provide any additional requirement of land by the BSF in the border areas.
He claimed that the people gave their "appropriate retort" through the democratic process.
The Trinamool Congress lost to the BJP in the 2026 assembly elections in the State.

articles.title: Assam OIL facility fire: death toll rises to four as another injured dies; four suspended
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident

The toll in the fire incident at an Oil India Ltd (OIL) facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district increased to four with another injured worker succumbing on Sunday (November 8, 2026), while the PSU has suspended all four of its personnel who were in charge of the site, officials said.
Three people who were also injured in the blaze on Friday (November 6, 2026) are undergoing treatment in a critical condition.
All the victims were employees of Spectron Engineering Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company engaged by OIL.
One person was killed in the fire on the day of the incident, while two died the next day.
A mechanical helper, Sailen Gogoi, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital here, died during the day, taking the toll to four, the official said.
A fire had broken out on November 6 after an explosion during maintenance work at OIL's intermediate tank farm (ITF) in Tengakhat, the public sector undertaking said in a statement.
An ITF is a facility where petroleum products are temporarily stored in tanks before being transferred for further processing or transportation.
Meanwhile, OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident, another official said.

The committee has put all four OIL employees who were in-charge of the ITF, including three officers, on suspension, he said. "They were placed under suspension until the investigation is over," the official added.
The PSU has announced an ex-gratia of ₹10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person.
Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma were closely monitoring the situation, the PSU said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
Mr. Sonowal, who is the Lok Sabha MP from Dibrugarh, called OIL CMD Ranjit Rath to take stock of the situation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Sonowal, who is the Lok Sabha MP from Dibrugarh, called OIL CMD Ranjit Rath to take stock of the situation.

articles.title: NGT issues notice to Tirunelveli Collector over threats to Tamirabharani fish species
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: National Green Tribunal takes suo motu cognisance of The Hindu report

The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss.

Taking suo motu cognisance of a report, titled ‘Tamirabharani’s Endemic Fish Face Threats From Pollution, Habitat Loss’, published in The Hindu on September 28, the Bench, comprising Justice Arun Kumar Tyagi and expert members A. Senthil Vel and Afroz Ahamed, directed that the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, the Central Pollution Control Board’s Regional Office in Chennai, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE), and Agasthyamalai Community Conservation Centre (ACCC) be impleaded as respondents, besides the Collector.

The order said: “The above news item attracts the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and prima facie raises substantial questions relating to the environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.”
The Bench directed the Registry to list the matter before the Southern Bench of the Tribunal, Chennai, on January 22, 2027, as the cause of action had arisen within its territorial jurisdiction.

It also directed the respondents to file their responses before the Bench at least one day ahead of the date of hearing. The Hindu had reported that 125 fish species had been identified in upstream, midstream and lower estuarine stretches of the river. Seven of them are endemic to the Tamirabharani.

Pollution, habitat destruction, loss of riparian vegetation, invasive fish and aquatic plants, use of soaps and shampoos by people bathing in the river, rituals performed on its banks, dumping of puja materials and clothes, and discharge of untreated sewage have contributed to the decline in fish populations.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 08 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

NGT issues notice to Tirunelveli Collector over threats to Tamirabharani fish species

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

National Green Tribunal takes suo motu cognisance of The Hindu report

The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss.

Taking suo motu cognisance of a report, titled ‘Tamirabharani’s Endemic Fish Face Threats From Pollution, Habitat Loss’, published in The Hindu on September 28, the Bench, comprising Justice Arun Kumar Tyagi and expert members A. Senthil Vel and Afroz Ahamed, directed that the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, the Central Pollution Control Board’s Regional Office in Chennai, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE), and Agasthyamalai Community Conservation Centre (ACCC) be impleaded as respondents, besides the Collector.

The order said: “The above news item attracts the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and prima facie raises substantial questions relating to the environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.”

The Bench directed the Registry to list the matter before the Southern Bench of the Tribunal, Chennai, on January 22, 2027, as the cause of action had arisen within its territorial jurisdiction.

It also directed the respondents to file their responses before the Bench at least one day ahead of the date of hearing. The Hindu had reported that 125 fish species had been identified in upstream, midstream and lower estuarine stretches of the river. Seven of them are endemic to the Tamirabharani.

Pollution, habitat destruction, loss of riparian vegetation, invasive fish and aquatic plants, use of soaps and shampoos by people bathing in the river, rituals performed on its banks, dumping of puja materials and clothes, and discharge of untreated sewage have contributed to the decline in fish populations.

1. Core Context & Background: National Green Tribunal takes suo motu cognisance of The Hindu report

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Pollution, habitat destruction, loss of riparian vegetation, invasive fish and aquatic plants, use of soaps and shampoos by people bathing in the river, rituals performed on its banks, dumping of puja materials and clothes, and discharge of untreated sewage have contributed to the decline in fish populations.

articles.title: ‘Dimagi Naxals’ instigating people against Constitution: PM Modi as Maoists eliminated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Celebrating Diwali with CRPF personnel in Bastar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country must “identify and defeat” ideological supporters of Naxalism who have “infiltrated” parties and organisations

Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

“We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country,” Mr. Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with the men and women in uniform. The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.

“Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added. The government, he said, took decisions that “dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists”.

On Independence Day in August 2026, Mr. Modi had also referred to “dimagi Naxals”, saying the country had succeeded in removing armed Naxalism but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.

Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, Mr. Modi said it had not been easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 States were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill, thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, and there were around 2,000 Naxalite attacks annually, he said.

“This land had become soaked in the blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments. Between 2004 and 2013, more security personnel were killed every year than the number of Naxalites eliminated, he said.

“Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed. No country can function with such an approach towards its enemies... The lack of political will that the country faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” he said.

The morale of security forces began changing after 2014, Mr. Modi said, adding that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel lost his life while on duty over the past year. “This is a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will. This is a victory of your valour, courage and restraint,” he said.

The Prime Minister said the government had taken tough decisions to strengthen national security, including measures not widely known.

“These decisions and efforts dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and secessionists. The fake currency nexus was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply lines. As a result, the supply of weapons was stopped, and the recruitment of Naxalites was curbed,” he said.

articles.title: Turkey, Azerbaijan leaders vow unity after tensions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Turkic-speaking allies describe their relationship as "one nation, two states" and, despite the friction, remain closely bound by military and energy ties

Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that their countries' alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours.
Tensions flared in September, when Baku revised school uniform regulations to prohibit clothing deemed incompatible with secular education, effectively barring Islamic headscarves in classrooms.
Mr. Erdogan's government has dismantled restrictions on hijabs in Turkey.

Azerbaijan's move sparked protests at home and drew criticism from Mr. Erdogan's Islamist-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP). Presidential adviser Oktay Saral demanded that Azerbaijan reverse the restrictions.
Baku also declared 31 Turkish nationals, including an Opposition lawmaker and party leaders, persona non grata over critical social media posts.

Mr. Erdogan subsequently dismissed Mr. Saral, but Mr. Aliyev stayed away from an October 30 summit of Turkic leaders in Ankara — despite a personal invitation from Mr. Erdogan. Instead, he sent Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Mr. Erdogan arrived in the country's Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago.
A guard of honour lined up at the airport, where Mr. Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva, welcomed Mr. Erdogan and his wife Ms. Emine.
"With the permission of Almighty God, our unity will endure forever," Mr. Erdogan told a joint press conference with Mr. Aliyev.
"This unity of hearts, which we describe with the motto 'One Nation, Two States,' is an everlasting torch that draws strength from our shared past and illuminates our future."
Mr. Aliyev said the alliance — "an important factor across a vast geographical area" — remained unshaken.
"Together, Azerbaijan and Turkey are even stronger," he said, adding that Mr. Erdogan's visit "shows the whole world our unity".

articles.title: Train collision in Egypt's Giza kills four, injures 88 others: Health Ministry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza's Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt's worst-ever rail disaster
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday (November 8, 2026), derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities.
Egypt's railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
The Health Ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area.
State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident "with great concern", and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to "hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".
Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.
Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza's Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt's worst-ever rail disaster.
In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.
Egypt's 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

articles.title: 23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Fighting in the Ruweng administrative area has left 23 dead and thousands displaced, officials said, as South Sudan heads towards elections on December 22

Four weeks of clashes between South Sudan government and opposition forces in the north of the impoverished country have left 23 people dead while thousands have fled the conflict zone, authorities and police said Sunday.

Hundreds of people have died in clashes across South Sudan in recent weeks between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and those of detained former vice president Riek Machar and other ethnic unrest, as the world's youngest country heads towards national elections scheduled for December 22.
Ruweng administrative area's information minister Tony Chol Ayat told AFP that fighters from Riek Machar's SPLA-IO force had entered Ruweng from neighbouring Unity state.
He said fighting between October 4 and Thursday this week had left 23 dead and 17 wounded. The toll was confirmed by two police sources.
Chol Ayat said that more than 100,000 people had fled the fighting while one of the police sources confirmed "thousands" had left the area.
A resident in Ruweng told AFP that SPLA-IO fighters had started fighting and that "the government built up forces on the front lines and the rebel armies were repelled".
Another Ruweng resident said there were fears of heightened conflict. Both spoke on condition of anonymity.
A South Sudan army spokesman would not comment on events, while Riek Machar's forces did not respond to an AFP query.

Independent since 2011, South Sudan is one of the world's poorest countries with widespread corruption. Saalva Kiir and Riek Machar's forces fought a civil war from 2013 to 2018 that left more than 400,000 dead.

The country's first presidential and legislative election has already been postponed several times and a UN human rights commission, which has accused the country's elite of siphoning off billions of dollars of oil revenues, has said an election in current tensions could unleash widespread new conflict.

articles.title: Poland calls Krakow shooting rampage 'terrorist' attack
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, says an Interior Ministry spokeswoman

Poland on Sunday (November 88, 2026) launched a terrorism probe as mourners brought candles and flowers to Krakow's Main Market Square in tribute to six people killed by a gunman who authorities said was "fascinated by far-right ideologies".
The 24-year-old Polish man opened fire at random on Saturday (November 7) in the historic centre of the country's second city, in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk called an act of "terrorism".
A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, an Interior Ministry spokeswoman said.
Three more bodies were found at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, around 150 kilometres (95 miles) northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.
The gunman was wounded in a shootout with police and is in critical condition in hospital. The National Prosecutor's Office said it had launched a terrorism investigation.
"I'm absolutely devastated," Weronika Filar, 27, a Krakow resident, told AFP on Sunday (November 8).
"It's one of the safest places on Earth genuinely... I did not expect anything like this to happen to us," she said. "Our city will never be the same."
"We've heard of various incidents of this sort happening elsewhere in Europe," Krzysztof Stepien, a 28-year-old part-time city guide told AFP.
"Nothing like this has ever happened here, and I hope it never will again," Stepien said.
Two police officers were wounded as they desperately chased the suspect, who was masked and dressed in military garb, including a bullet-proof vest.
The man left his car at an intersection and started shooting at the officers with a semi-automatic rifle, according to police.
Social media images showed the two police firing at the gunman, with one managing to wound him despite his own injuries.

articles.title: Israel Defence Minister says 'mission not complete' on Iran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: "Concerning Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons — alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger," says Mr. Katz
Israel is not finished with Iran, its Defence Minister said Sunday (November 8, 2026), as he also warned Tehran's Lebanese ally Hezbollah to hold fire in any resumption of war.
Defence Minister Israel Katz renewed charges that Iran — attacked twice since last year in major Israeli-U.S. bombing campaigns — is pursuing nuclear weapons, a claim that Tehran denies.

"Concerning Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons — alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger," Mr. Katz said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is fighting for his political life, has repeatedly threatened new strikes against Iran in recent weeks.

But it remains unclear if he has the support of U.S. President Donald Trump, his close ally, who suffered a major rebuke from voters in elections on Tuesday (November 10), in part over anger against the war.

Israel's Channel 12 reported Friday that Mr. Netanyahu and the Mossad intelligence service attempted an operation against Iran on the eve of Israel's own October 27 election but that the United States found out and stopped it.
Mr. Netanyahu has ordered a multi-nation war since the unprecedented attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, by Hamas, the Palestinian militant group in Gaza backed by Iran's clerical state.

Israel has devastated Gaza and has invaded Lebanon, after Hezbollah fired on Israel in solidarity with Iran. Israel has also moved past a former ceasefire line to occupy part of historic adversary Syria after the fall in 2024 of longtime leader Bashar al-Assad.

"We will not withdraw from the security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, and if the terrorist organisation Hezbollah chooses to join Iran in an attack on Israel, it will suffer extremely severe blows," Mr. Katz said.
Mr. Netanyahu suffered losses in the October 27 election, with his rival Gadi Eisenkot tasked with forming a new government.

Eisenkot has warned Israel's military that Mr. Netanyahu has no mandate and that it should not go to war for his "political needs", although the former army chief has largely supported Mr. Netanyahu's war decisions.

"We may argue, and we may disagree, but when the security of the state is at stake, we must know how to rise above our disputes," said Mr. Katz, who was speaking at a ceremony for Israeli troops who died in a 1956 attack on Egypt.

articles.title: Habitual offender arrested for murdering 65-year-old woman in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kengeri police have arrested a habitual offender for allegedly murdering a 65-year-old woman who was sleeping outside a temple and robbing her of cash and a gold ring in Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout.
The deceased, Narayanamma, was found dead in front of the Pataladamma Temple at Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout, Konasandra, within Kengeri police station limits, on November 3.
According to the police, Narayanamma had left her house due to family problems and had been sleeping outside the temple for the past few days.
A local resident who noticed her body informed her son, who arrived at the spot and identified her. The Kengeri police initially registered an unnatural death report based on his complaint.

However, following the post-mortem examination and information gathered during the investigation, police suspected that she had been murdered and robbed. A murder case was subsequently registered on Thursday.
During the investigation, police apprehended a suspicious person moving around Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout on Friday. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to the crime.
The accused reportedly told investigators that he had noticed Narayanamma sleeping alone and decided to rob her to arrange money to fund his vices.
In the early hours of November 3, he allegedly went to the spot, covered her mouth, assaulted her and robbed her of the cash she was carrying and a gold ring before fleeing, leaving her dead.

Police said the accused has a criminal history and was previously involved in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and robbery cases at Girinagar and Cottonpet police stations.
Further investigation and interrogation are under way, police said.

articles.title: P.T. Usha complains to IOA electoral officer over WhatsApp campaign for SOM polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian Olympic Association president alleged former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message seeking votes for four candidates ahead of Monday’s election

Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president P.T. Usha has lodged a complaint with the Electoral Officer alleging that former archer Dola Banerjee violated the Model Code of Conduct by circulating a WhatsApp message soliciting votes for a panel of four candidates in Monday’s (November 9, 2026) Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections.

In her complaint, Usha objected to a WhatsApp message circulated through an account bearing Banerjee’s name, seeking support for the ‘New Bharat Panel’ and asking voters to elect four named candidates, along with their ballot serial numbers and roll numbers.

Usha cited Clause 1.9 of the Model Code of Conduct, issued on October 30, 2026, which states that the promotion of a candidate shall exclude any form of publicity, including the use of new media or social networks. She contended that the circulation of the message amounted to targeted solicitation of votes through social media, and appeared to fall within the ambit of the clause. The complaint also referred to Clauses 1.2 and 1.3, which require candidates to conduct their campaigns fairly, with dignity and moderation, and to show due respect to other candidates.

Usha has urged the election authorities to examine the communication, establish the circumstances under which it was created and circulated, and seek an explanation from the persons concerned. She has also sought appropriate action under the applicable election rules if a violation is established, along with directions to ensure a level playing field for all candidates.

With polling scheduled from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 9, 2026, Usha has sought urgent intervention and a decision before voting begins. A screenshot of the WhatsApp message and a copy of the Model Code of Conduct were enclosed with the complaint.

articles.title: Revanth celebrates Deepavali with Indiramma house beneficiary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ministers, MLAs asked to spend festival with poor families who received houses; 2.21 lakh houses completed under scheme

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy along with Ministers and MLA celebrated Deepavali with a beneficiary of the Indiramma housing scheme at Parsapur village in Kodangal mandal on Sunday (November 8, 2026), in an initiative aimed at highlighting the government’s flagship housing programme for poor families.

The Chief Minister inaugurated the newly constructed house of Goripalli Sumitra and Srinivas, presented new clothes to the family, and had a traditional Deepavali meal of fine rice at their residence. Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar and Ministers Seethakka, Jupally Krishna Rao, Damodar Rajanarasimha and other public representatives joined the family for lunch.

The programme, titled ‘Maa Indiramma Intlo Deepavali’ (Deepavali in Our Indiramma Home), was conceived by Mr. Revanth Reddy to take the government’s housing initiative to the people and celebrate the festival with families who were allotted the houses.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and his Cabinet colleagues have lunch at the residence of a Indiramma house beneficiary in Kodangal constituency on November 8, 2026. Photo credit: Special Arrangement.

He had asked Ministers, MLAs and other elected representatives to spend Deepavali with beneficiaries of the scheme in their respective constituencies. The idea was to make the festival a celebration with poor families who had received permanent homes through government assistance, rather than confining the programme to official celebrations.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and his Cabinet colleagues present new clothes to a family of Indiramma house beneficiary in Kodangal constituency on November 8, 2026 as a part of Deepavali celebrations. Photo credit: Special Arrangement
The beneficiaries are picked up in an open lot without any interference of political leader, and the programmes are held in open spaces in the presence of all those who applied for the scheme.

The State has committed around ₹40,000 crore towards the two phases and the proposed urban housing programme. Separately, official housing department data available in October showed that ₹7,634 crore had been released to beneficiaries towards construction assistance.

The Indiramma Indlu scheme was one of the key promises made by the Congress before the 2023 Assembly elections where the party had promised to provide a house to every eligible homeless family extending a financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to construct a house.
The houses have two rooms, a kitchen and a toilet. In the first phase, the government sanctioned 4.5 lakh houses, with 3,500 houses earmarked for each Assembly constituency.

articles.title: Rajajinagar murders: Two more bodies recovered near Chamundi hills in Mysuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues

In a fresh development in the brutal murder of seven members of a family, Rajajinagar Police have recovered two more bodies, suspected to be those of Shivakumar and his wife Divya — the accused Indushekhar’s brother-in-law and sister-in-law — near the foothills of Chamundi Hills in Mysuru, on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Police conducted a spot mahazar of the spot with the accused while recovering the bodies.
With this development, five bodies have been traced so far in the case, while the search for the remaining two continues.

DCP, North Division said that two more dead bodies found near Chamundi hill forest area are said to be of Shivakumar and Divya. Another special police team has been deployed to Shiradi Ghat, where it is conducting searches for the two more missing bodies, he said.

On Saturday (November 7, 2026), police recovered the bodies of the accused’s wife, Sunita, and mother-in-law, Rupavathi, from a forest area in Salem, Tamil Nadu. The body of a young boy was earlier recovered near the foothills of Nandi Hills and has already been cremated.

According to the investigation, Indushekhar allegedly murdered seven of his relatives, including his wife, over a period of 15 days. He is suspected to have packed the bodies in gunny bags, transported them in his car and dumped them at different locations, including the foothills of Nandi Hills, a forest area in Salem, the foothills of Chamundi Hills and Shiradi Ghat.

The accused, who is currently in police custody, is being subjected to intensive interrogation as investigators try to establish the sequence of murders, the motive and the locations where the remaining bodies were disposed of.

articles.title: UK Hindu family takes legal action after school objects to boy wearing tilak
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The parents of a nine-year-old boy have approached the UK High Court, alleging religious discrimination after he was prevented from wearing the sacred Tilak-Chandlo to school

The parents of a nine-year-old British Hindu boy, who was withdrawn from his primary school in London after it objected to him wearing a tilak on his forehead, have initiated legal proceedings in the UK High Court.

The boy, who belongs to the Swaminarayan faith tradition, had attended Vicar’s Green Primary School in west London since 2021 and worn his religious marking, known as the Tilak-Chandlo, without difficulty.
However, the school objected to the practice in late 2025, triggering a dispute that eventually led his parents to withdraw him from the school and pursue legal action.
“As parents, it has been heartbreaking to see our son go through this simply because he wanted to practise his faith,” the parents said in a statement released by their legal team this weekend.
“He had worn his Tilak-Chandlo to school for years without difficulty, and we never imagined that something so sacred to our family would become a source of distress,” they said.
“Our son was just an ordinary little boy who enjoyed learning and spending time with his friends. His religious marking did not hurt anyone or prevent him from being a good pupil.

“We have always taught our children to respect every religion, and we simply ask that the same respect be shown to ours. We hope that no other child will have to choose between their education and their faith,” they added.
The family is represented by Ashray Law, which has filed proceedings alleging religious discrimination under the UK’s Equality Act 2010 and breaches of rights protected by the Human Rights Act 1998.
The case, filed in the High Court of England and Wales, seeks £25,000 in damages. The proceedings are ongoing, and the allegations remain in dispute.
“This case goes beyond one child or one school. It raises important questions about religious freedom and equality in British education,” said Ambrish Limbachia, director of Ashray Law.
“No child should feel compelled to choose between their faith and their education. We hope these proceedings will help clarify the rights of children from all religious backgrounds,” he said.

The Tilak-Chandlo is a U-shaped marking, usually made with sandalwood paste and a small red circle of kumkum powder in the centre. It symbolises devotion to God and humility among followers of the Swaminarayan faith.

articles.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing Dutch government on Gaza, Israel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Organisers of the “Red Line” demonstration called for stricter trade sanctions, a halt to arms sales, and an official declaration that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide

Tens of thousands of people, many of them dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in a mass demonstration aimed at pressing the Dutch government to take more decisive action against Israel over Gaza.

The organisers of the “Red Line” demonstrations in the Netherlands called for measures including stricter trade sanctions on Israel, officially declaring that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide, and halting all arms sales to Israel. The Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organisers, said in an online post that more than 200,000 people joined the march.

“What is happening there is inhumane,” said Mike van Dongen, as he walked in the huge throng. He was critical of the Dutch government’s actions. “As far as I’m concerned, they are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”

As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood on a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoed his cry as they passed.

Israel strongly rejects suggestions it is committing genocide in Gaza in its military campaign, which followed the attacks by Hamas-led militants in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. Militants killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostages.

Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and destroyed much of Gaza. More than 1,550 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed by the Israeli military since a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas began in October 2025, according to the territory’s Health Ministry.
The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, does not distinguish between civilians and militants, though it says women and children make up roughly half of the dead.

The campaign in Gaza has strained relations between the Netherlands and Israel. The Dutch Foreign Minister resigned last year after failing to secure new sanctions against Israel. Since then, a new minority coalition government has taken power and introduced an import ban on products from Israeli settlements, which the Dutch government and most of the international community consider illegal, a move that provoked a diplomatic spat with Israel.

Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who took part in a march last year but was not present on Sunday, defended his government’s actions at his weekly press conference on Friday (November 6, 2026). “Every single day and every single week, we do what we can to alleviate the terrible situation there,” he said.

He added that his administration was “exerting greater political and diplomatic pressure” on Israel to abide by its agreements on Gaza. At the same time, he said, the government was applying more pressure on Hamas and other organisations that continue to carry out “various operations that endanger the safety of ordinary Israelis.”

articles.title: Eisenkot warns of Israel crisis as he seeks to replace Netanyahu’s government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: isenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority

Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday (November 8, 2026) of forming a government , reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu's allies as he warned the veteran Prime Minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Mr. Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Mr. Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

"We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel," Mr. Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie, said at a ceremony at the Presidential office.
"We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps."

Mr. Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic Prime Minister — a community mostly descended from West Asian or North African Jews — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe.

Mr. Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, having led the country on and off for nearly two decades. He has taken the country in a sharply rightward direction and led wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran since the October 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas.
Both Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Herzog acknowledged Israel's growing isolation under Mr. Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court.

In the United States, the most vital ally of Israel, Democrats on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) swept elections with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war which Mr. Netanyahu launched with President Donald Trump.
"We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed," Mr. Eisenkot said.
Mr. Eisenkot appealed to Mr. Netanyahu's Likud Party as well as the far-right party of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to join — but only with himself as Prime Minister.
"My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment," he said.
In consultations last week with Mr. Herzog, Mr. Eisenkot received recommendations from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers, against 46 for Mr. Netanyahu.

articles.title: South Africa's ANC suffers worst election result as decline continues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted

South Africa's African National Congress party faced its worst election results ever on Sunday (November 8, 2026) and a new low point on its gradual decline in popularity as voters rebuked it for a failure to deliver basic services like water and electricity in towns and cities.

The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted. The final results were expected late on Sunday (November 8, 2026), according to the Independent Electoral Commission.

The ANC remained the largest party by total share in an election involving hundreds of parties, but the Democratic Alliance that is its main Opposition had received around 25% of votes in the near-complete count.

That brought closer to reality the once-unthinkable notion that the ANC that led South Africa out of the white minority rule of apartheid and delivered freedom in 1994 under Mandela might one day not be its biggest party. It used to command 70% of the vote.

The ANC's popularity has declined for more than a decade. It won 45% support in the last local elections in 2021, the first time it had dropped below 50% in any election. In 2024, it then lost its Parliamentary majority for the first time in a national election, which brought about a coalition national government and a seismic shift in South African politics.

The ANC was on course Sunday (November 8, 2026) for a steep drop of about 15 percentage points from the last local elections and the loss of approximately one-third of its support from five years ago.
“If anyone has not heard what the people are saying in this election, then you are lost,” said ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula. “This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC.”
He said the results called for the ANC “to be humble, to hear our people and respect them,” and to “earn again through service and not through slogans the trust people have lent to others.”
DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said his party — which was around 20% points behind the ANC in the 2024 national election — had now “taken a big step forward” in its aim to be South Africa's biggest.
But, while the ANC's popularity has dropped sharply, no single party has overtaken it as the vote has fragmented among many parties on a local and national scale.

Another seven major parties shared around 30% of the vote in these local elections, which had more than 500 parties contesting and many picking up small shares. The MK Party led by former South African President Jacob Zuma, who broke away from the ANC and was expelled by it, held the third-largest share of votes at around 10%.

Voters across South Africa have long expressed frustration over failed public services that have left many cities and towns with regular water and electricity outages, broken roads and streetlights, and uncollected refuse.

articles.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The devastating result leaves Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure

U.S. President Donald Trump vowed a political comeback on Sunday (November 8, 2026) after his Republican Party lost control of both houses of Congress in midterm elections that amounted to an unequivocal repudiation of his turbulent Presidency.

The devastating result leaves Mr. Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year 'lame duck' period of his White House tenure, while opening the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress into the President, his family and senior members of his administration.

"America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election," Mr. Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote.
"But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!"
While the resounding election loss last Tuesday (November 3, 2026) has prompted soul-searching among Republican lawmakers, Mr. Trump has sounded defiant.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), he appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signalling a bare-knuckle fightback.
Democrats, meanwhile, have pledged to hold the Trump administration to account and fight against Mr. Miller, the architect of Mr. Trump's tough immigration policy.

Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to "lawyer up," Mr. Trump said on Saturday (November 8, 2026) he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to "extortion."
That stance stoked a war of words between top Republicans and Democrats on U.S. political shows on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Mr. Trump and now head of the Justice Department, vowed to actively defend Mr. Trump and senior members of his administration.

"You have members of Congress who, after Tuesday (November 3, 2026), have done nothing but threaten everything that's happening in this administration," Mr. Blanche told CNN , citing impeachment threats against Mr. Miller after his appointment.
"If they try to come after Stephen Miller...instead of actually just conducting oversight and leading, of course the Department of Justice will be there to defend him."

articles.title: Thick smog blankets Delhi on Deepavali night, AQI at 20 stations ‘severe’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days

A smoky haze hung over Delhi on Deepavali night, blurring streetlights and blanketing neighbourhoods as celebrations intensified across the capital, pushing air quality at 20 monitoring stations into the ‘severe’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index standing at 371 at 10 p.m..

The haze grew denser as the evening progressed, with smoke from firecrackers hanging over roads and residential neighbourhoods. The smell of burnt crackers lingered in the air, while visibility dropped in several parts of the capital and residents reported difficulty breathing.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Delhi air pollution: Capital sees ‘very poor’ AQI on Deepavali as GRAP 3 curbs continue

Despite restrictions on bursting firecrackers, several parts of Delhi continued to witness their use on Sunday evening (November 8, 2026), with reports of fireworks emerging from areas, including Pitampura, Burari, Mayur Vihar and parts of Lutyens’ Delhi.
Ahead of Deepavali, the Delhi government had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.
The District Magistrate (East), in an order, had permitted the bursting of green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m..

Residents reported that firecrackers were being burst in outer Delhi’s Pitampura and Burari, with the intensity particularly high in Burari. Similar reports came from Mayur Vihar, while people in the Bishambardas Marg area and Lutyens’ Delhi said fireworks continued, although the intensity had reduced slightly.

Of the 59 monitoring stations, 19 were in the 'severe' category at 7 p.m., seven in the 'poor' category, and the remaining 33 in the 'very poor' category. Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 460.
The city's average AQI for the day settled at 376 in the 'very poor' category, compared to 369 on Saturday, amid a layer of smog and reduced visibility.
The court prohibited bursting of firecrackers within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and other notified silence zones.

Only CSIR-NEERI-certified green firecrackers were permitted for sale, with the administration directing that they be sold exclusively at locations designated by the Delhi Police. The administration had also announced joint patrolling and enforcement teams comprising district officials and Delhi Police personnel to check unauthorised sale and use of prohibited firecrackers.
Meanwhile, the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
